title: Start here
text: Marine voice, a validated identity, and a vessel on the map. Your Bridge brings them together.

title: Installation
text:
Before you start 
 You need Raspberry Pi OS 64-bit or Ubuntu, a working AIS-catcher viewer and  a second RTL-SDR  for marine voice. The documented Ubuntu targets are 24.04 and 26.04. 
 AIS-catcher keeps its own receiver. The Bridge uses only the voice receiver you explicitly select and reads AIS data without taking over AIS-catcher. 
 The default AIS feed is  http://127.0.0.1:8119/ships.json  on the same machine. Check that AIS-catcher is running first. 
 Install Stable 
 Open a terminal on your Pi or Ubuntu machine: 
  git clone --branch main https://github.com/EyeVisionsNL/AIS-ATIS-Bridge.git
cd AIS-ATIS-Bridge
sudo ./install.sh
  
 The installer sets up the Bridge service, RTLSDR-Airband runtime and updater. If RTLSDR-Airband is missing, it builds the pinned version. Give that step time to finish. 
 Open your dashboard 
 Open  http://<raspberry-pi-address>:8120  in your browser. Replace the placeholder with your Pi’s address; on the Pi itself, use  http://localhost:8120 . 
 Select the second receiver before saving. Continue with  First steps  for your first listening session. 
 Already installed? 
 Use  Updates  for dashboard updates or upgrading an older installation. Existing configuration is preserved by the installer. 
 What this project is for 
 This is a listening and identification tool. As the project README states, do not use it for navigation or safety. Reception depends on your hardware, antenna and local signals.

title: First steps
text:
Meet your Bridge 
 The dashboard puts receiver controls, recent transmissions, validated ATIS and updates together. Start with the receiver panel, then work your way across. 
   
  This project screenshot contains demonstration recordings and illustrative settings, not live reception. Click it to enlarge.  
 Get your first signal 
 
 In  Receiver , select the second RTL-SDR. Leave AIS-catcher’s dongle to AIS-catcher. 
 Choose  Fixed channel  and select a marine voice channel active in your area, or choose  Scan channels  and enable a small selection. 
 Start with  Smart Gain  and  Automatic (noise tracking)  squelch. 
 Click  Save and start  and check the receiver status. 
 Click  Audio: off  to listen, then adjust  Volume . 
 
 Sound comes from the device running your browser. There is no need to plug headphones into the Pi when you are browsing from your laptop. 
 Let a transmission finish 
 Recent recordings become available for replay after the signal ends. A validated ATIS identity appears only when a suitable ATIS transmission is successfully decoded; ordinary speech alone does not identify a ship. 
 Find the vessel 
 A fresh, unique AIS match enables  Show on AIS map . If no match appears, use  ATIS and AIS  to understand the checks. 
 Ready to explore?  Receiver and channels  explains scanning and RF settings, and  Audio and recordings  covers listening and replay.

title: Receiver & channels
text:
One receiver, one job 
 Select the dongle dedicated to marine voice. The Bridge requires an explicit receiver selection; AIS-catcher retains exclusive ownership of its own dongle. 
 Fixed channel or scan? 
 
 
 
 Mode 
 What it does 
 A useful starting point 
 
 
 
 
 Fixed channel 
 Stays on your selected channel 
 Checking a known local voice channel 
 
 
 Scan channels 
 Scans the channels you enable 
 Following several nearby marine channels 
 
 
 
 Enable at least one channel for scanning, then click  Save and start  after changing settings.  Stop receiver  stops the voice receiver. 
 Smart Gain 
 Smart Gain briefly probes up to twelve selected channels, chooses a supported gain step between 0 and 25.4 dB, then holds that gain fixed while receiving. If the probe cannot run or finds no clear signal, it falls back to 12.5 dB. 
 Choose  Manual  for your own fixed tuner gain. The input accepts 0–49.6 dB. More gain does not always improve reception; adjust for your antenna and local conditions. 
 Squelch 
  Automatic (noise tracking)  uses the existing 4 dB SNR setting.  Manual (dBFS)  accepts whole-number thresholds from −100 to −1 dBFS; its default is −47 dBFS. 
 A higher threshold admits stronger signals only. Too low a threshold can leave the scanner listening to noise instead of moving on. These controls apply to both fixed and scan modes. 
 Scan speed 
 Set  Scan speed  from 100 to 500 ms per channel in 50 ms steps. Lower values scan faster; 200 ms per channel is the default. Begin there and adjust once you have confirmed reception. 
 Marine channel workbook 
 The 0.1.13 voice catalog contains  133 unique analogue receive carriers , including relevant duplex sides and Dutch supplementary/private channels. 
 
  Marine channel list  downloads the supplied workbook. 
  Export current  saves your current channel list. 
  Import Excel  reads a compatible workbook, including an SDRCC workbook; Aviation rows are ignored and Marine rows retained. 
 
 The supported Marine receive range is 155.775–162.600 MHz. AIS, DSC and other data-only allocations are excluded from Voice. AIS reception remains the job of AIS-catcher. 
 When older channel banks migrate, the Bridge matches by frequency, keeps scan choices and custom voice channels, and removes obsolete data-only entries.

title: Audio & recordings
text:
Listen live 
 Start the receiver with  Save and start , then click  Audio: off . Audio is off whenever the page loads and needs a click to begin. 
 Adjust  Volume  on the dashboard; 0% mutes playback. Sound plays through the browser device’s speakers or headphones, using live mono 16 kHz audio from the same receiver feed used for ATIS decoding. 
 Replay the last transmission 
  Recent Marine transmissions  keeps up to four squelch-gated recordings. Each can be up to two minutes long, with WAV replay available after the signal ends. 
 These recordings live in memory. They are not a permanent archive and disappear when the Bridge process restarts. 
 Listen less, keep receiving 
 Turning live audio off does not stop decoding, scanning or recording. Use  Stop receiver  when you want to stop the voice receiver itself. 
 No sound? 
 
 Confirm the receiver is running and the selected channel has a signal. 
 Click the audio button; page loads do not start listening automatically. 
 Check dashboard volume and your browser device’s output volume. 
 If the browser suspended a background tab, click Audio again. 
 Review squelch and gain in  Receiver and channels . 
 
 No recording during a quiet period is normal: capture depends on squelch opening for a transmission.

title: ATIS & AIS map
text:
From voice to vessel 
 The Bridge receives marine VHF audio, validates a 10-digit ATIS identity, and compares it with vessels in AIS-catcher’s local feed. ATIS supplies the identity; AIS supplies vessel information and position. 
 ATIS validation uses RAINWAT symbol checks, time diversity and ECC. A decoded number is not automatically accepted as a vessel match. 
 Why a match can be missing 
 The Bridge requires a fresh validated ATIS record, a unique matching vessel, a valid MMSI and position, and sufficiently recent AIS data. AIS records can be up to  30 minutes old , matching AIS-catcher’s default retention window. That allowance does not remove the ATIS freshness checks. 
 Ambiguous, stale or invalid records do not trigger map selection. A ship being audible does not guarantee that it also appears in the current AIS feed. 
 Dutch callsign fallback 
 When standard matching finds no candidate, Dutch ATIS identities with MID 244, 245 or 246 can also match an exact normalized AIS callsign. The result is reported as  callsign_exact_fallback . 
 Duplicate callsigns and invalid or stale data remain rejected. An ambiguous or rejected standard match is not bypassed, and foreign callsigns are not guessed. 
 Open the AIS map 
 Click  Show on AIS map  for a fresh, uniquely matched vessel. Allow the map pop-up when prompted by your browser. 
 Click  Auto: off  to enable automatic following. The same named AIS-catcher window is reused for subsequent fresh matches. Turning Auto off stops following; closing the map also stops Auto. 
 Viewer integration 
 The installer copies the optional viewer plugin when  /etc/AIS-catcher/plugins  exists. Restart the AIS-catcher viewer afterward. A selected vessel card then offers  ATIS Bridge , opening the local Bridge page. 
 The defaults are  http://127.0.0.1:8119/ships.json  for the feed and  http://127.0.0.1:8119/  for the viewer. If the local viewer uses a different port or path, adjust  ais_ships_url  and  ais_viewer_url  in  /etc/ais-atis-bridge/config.json . Both must use a localhost URL. The map link replaces localhost with the browser-facing hostname.

title: Updates
text:
Update from the dashboard 
 
 Open  Bridge updates . 
 Choose  Stable  for  main  or  Beta  for  develop . 
 Click  Check for updates . 
 Review the available version and click  Install update . 
 Let the Bridge restart, then refresh the dashboard and check its version. 
 
 The updater verifies SHA-256 hashes, backs up installed application files and runs a health check. A failed health check triggers rollback. 
 Your settings stay yours 
 Receiver selection, mode, channels, gain, squelch and viewer settings are preserved. Configuration lives at  /etc/ais-atis-bridge/config.json , outside the application update. 
 The release-channel preference is saved independently of receiver settings. An explicit switch between Stable and Beta can install the selected branch even if its version is equal or older, provided that branch has an update manifest. Older releases within the currently installed channel remain blocked. 
 Upgrade an older checkout 
 Run the installer once to install the updater and service changes: 
  cd ~/AIS-ATIS-Bridge
git fetch origin
git switch main
git pull --ff-only origin main
sudo ./install.sh
  
 Preserve any local edits to tracked files before switching or pulling. For Beta, use  develop  instead of  main  in both branch commands. 
 “No new privileges” update error 
 Older service settings could block the updater helper. Run the terminal upgrade above once to repair those settings, then refresh the dashboard. The blocked updater cannot repair its own service configuration. 
 Future compatible releases can use the dashboard update button again.

title: Troubleshooting
text:
Dashboard will not open 
 Check that you are using the Pi’s address and port  8120 , and that your browser can reach that machine. On the Pi, inspect the service: 
  systemctl status ais-atis-bridge --no-pager
journalctl -u ais-atis-bridge -n 100 --no-pager
  
 The logs are useful when reporting a startup or receiver problem. 
 Receiver missing or stopped 
 Confirm that a second dongle is connected and selected. Do not select the receiver already used by AIS-catcher. Check the service log for USB access or RTLSDR-Airband errors. 
 Older releases had a receiver lifecycle problem corrected in 0.1.5. Upgrade an old installation before chasing that symptom further. 
 Scanner sticks on a channel 
 A manual squelch threshold below the noise floor can hold the scanner open. Try  Automatic (noise tracking)  or raise the manual threshold, then save and start again. 
 Speech, but no vessel match 
 Speech alone does not guarantee valid ATIS. Check whether an identity was validated, whether AIS-catcher’s local  ships.json  is available, and whether the candidate vessel has fresh, valid and unique AIS data. See  ATIS and AIS . 
 Map does not open 
 Allow the browser’s pop-up for the dashboard. Map controls require a fresh unique match. Confirm the viewer URL if you changed AIS-catcher’s port or path. 
 Recordings disappeared 
 The four recent recordings are held in memory and are cleared on a Bridge restart. This is expected. See  Audio and recordings . 
 Installer or update failed 
 Use  Updates  for the older updater repair and terminal upgrade. From a Stable source checkout, retry with: 
  cd ~/AIS-ATIS-Bridge
git pull --ff-only origin main
sudo ./install.sh
  
 Preserve local tracked-file edits first. The installer does not install or restart AIS-catcher itself. 
 Ask for help 
  Open an issue on GitHub  with your Bridge version, operating system, receiver model, selected mode, exact error and relevant service logs. Remove private details before posting.
